steps.body: Sixths and eighths cut the same journey into more, smaller jumps — and the more jumps there are, the shorter each one becomes.
steps.narration: Sixths and eighths cut the same journey into more, smaller jumps — and the more jumps there are, the shorter each one becomes.

commonPlacements.feedback: 2/6 is one jump short of halfway on a sixths line.
6/6 is the whole trip, landing on 1.

widget.successFeedback: 3/6 — three of six jumps, which is also exactly one half.
widget.lowFeedback: Jumps run FORWARD from 0, so a landing behind the target is short of it — count the jumps again.
widget.highFeedback: That is past the halfway mark — three of the six jumps is where 3/6 lands.

predict.reveal: Eight jumps must fit in the same distance as six, so each eighth is shorter than each sixth.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f sixths eighths really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f sixths eighths comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

widget.prompt: Which is bigger: a half or a third?

options.label: a half
options.feedback: Correct — more pieces in the same whole means each piece is smaller, so a half wins "bigger".

options.label: a third
options.feedback: a third is not the bigger one — compare how many pieces the whole was cut into.

options.label: they're the same size
options.feedback: They differ: the same whole cut into more pieces gives smaller pieces every time.

widget.prompt: A trail is 6/8 mile, then 1/8 mile more. Express the total as ?/8. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 names the piece size; adding same-size pieces changes only how MANY you have.
Multiplying the counts is not joining them — 6 pieces and 1 more pieces make 7.
